items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Vocabulary: words and phrases related to school things and school activities (school bag, pencil case, compass, pencil sharpener, rubber, calculator, subject, uniform, wear, put on).
 - Language function: talking about a special day at school and classroom objects.
 Skill Focus:
 - Listening
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Understand and use words and phrases related to school things and school activities.
 - Identify and use vocabulary about school things in simple contexts.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Identify the main ideas and specific information in a conversation about a special day.
 - Reading: Read the conversation to understand the main ideas and find specific information.
 - Speaking: Name and describe school things and talk about simple school activities.
 Value:
 - Develop a positive attitude towards school and school life.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Listen and repeat the target vocabulary.
 - Match the words with the pictures of school things.
 - Complete the sentences with teacher support.
 Core group:
 - Read the conversation and complete the T/F activity.
 - Complete the gap-fill activity using the conversation.
 - Look around the classroom and identify the school things.
 Challenge group:
 - Name more school things not shown in the textbook.
 - Describe the school things they use in different subjects using the target vocabulary.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Vocabulary matching activity.
 - Reading comprehension (True/False and gap-fill).
 - Pair/group speaking: naming and describing school things.
 - Exit ticket: Write the names of five school things you use at school.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Vocabulary: Vocabulary related to school (school lunch, English, history, homework, exercise, science, football, lessons, music).
 - Verbs collocations: Collocations with play, do, have, study.
 - Pronunciation: Sounds /ɑː/ and /ʌ/.
 Skill Focus:
 - Speaking
 - Listening
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Distinguish and use appropriate verbs (play, do, have, study) with school nouns.
 - Pronounce /ɑː/ and /ʌ/ accurately in words and sentences.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Listen and recognize words with /ɑː/ and /ʌ/ in sentences
 - Speaking: Produce /ɑː/ and /ʌ/ accurately and use verb collocations (with play, do, have, study) in context.
 Value:
 - Develop a positive attitude toward school activities and show confidence in communication.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match pictures with vocabulary words.
 - Complete sentence frames about school activities with given words.
 - Choral repetition of target sounds and words.
 Core group:
 - Categorize school nouns into correct verb columns with partners.
 - Pair practice asking and answering questions about school subjects.
 - Listen and underline target sounds in sentences.
 Challenge group:
 - Expand the word groups with more school activities.
 - Create short conversations about daily school routines using target collocations naturally.
 - Compare and explain the pronunciation differences of the target sounds.
items.assess:
- Vocabulary and pronunciation checklist.
 - Teacher observation during vocabulary grouping and pronunciation practice.
 - Exit ticket: Write 3 words with the target sounds.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Grammar: The present simple tense and adverbs of frequency (always, usually, sometimes, rarely, never).
 Skill Focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Use the present simple and adverbs of frequency to talk about actions that often happen.
 - Use the correct form of verbs and correct position of adverbs in sentences.
 Skills:
 - Reading: Read a short interview between Miss Nguyet and Duy to find specific verb forms.
 - Speaking: Ask and answer questions to interview a partner about their school activities.
 - Writing: Write sentences about daily routines using adverbs of frequency.
 Value:
 - Develop a positive attitude towards daily school routines.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Choose the correct words in sentences with teacher help.
 - Fill in the frequency adverbs pyramid using given words.
 Core group:
 - Complete multiple-choice activities.
 - Read the interview and write the correct form of verbs.
 - Work in pairs to interview a partner about school activities.
 Challenge group:
 - Write original sentences using adverbs of frequency about daily routines.
 - Make and answer extra interview questions with a partner fluently
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during pair work.
 - Multiple-choice activity checking.
 - Peer assessment during the interview task.
 - Exit ticket: Write three simple sentences using an adverb of frequency.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Vocabulary: countries, nationalities, ages, favourite food, animals and activities.
 - Reading focus: finding main ideas and deciding Right or Wrong.
 - Language pattern: like, love, enjoy and hate + noun / verb-ing.
 Skill Focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
 - Use simple words to talk about personal information and favourite things.
 - Use like, love, enjoy and hate in short sentences.
 Skills:
 - Reading: Read short profiles and find names, ages, countries and favourite things.
 - Speaking: Ask and answer simple questions about favourite things.
 Value:
 - Respect classmates’ different interests and preferences.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match key words about personal information, family and favourite things with pictures or simple meanings.
 - Use headings, pictures and underlined key words to find answers.
 - Complete selected reading questions with teacher prompts.
 Core group:
 - Complete the Student’s Book reading tasks independently.
 - Underline the words or sentences that support each answer.
 - Discuss one simple question about personal information, family and favourite things with a partner.
 Challenge group:
 - Write three short sentences to summarise the text.
 - Create two extra comprehension questions for a partner.
 - Compare the text with their own experience of personal information, family and favourite things.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Completed reading comprehension task.
 - Evidence-underlining check.
 - Exit ticket: one sentence about personal information, family and favourite things.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Vocabulary: numbers from teens to thousands.
 - Vocabulary: family members and relationships (parents, grandparents, aunt, uncle, cousin, brother, sister).
 - Vocabulary: possessions (diary, football boots, kitten, necklace, photograph, poster, smartphone, watch).
 - Personal information: first name, surname, age, nationality and marital status.
 Skill Focus:
 - Reading
 - Writing
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
 - Use numbers, family words and possession words in familiar contexts.
 - Give simple information about family members and personal belongings.
 Skills:
 - Reading: Read a family tree and a short family description to identify key information.
 - Writing: Write the target words and complete short sentences or descriptions about numbers, family relationships and possessions.
 - Speaking: Describe family relationships and favourite possessions in short sentences.
 Value:
 - Show care and respect when talking about family.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match the target words with pictures or definitions.
 - Complete sentences using a word bank.
 - Practise two model sentences with numbers from teens to thousands.
 Core group:
 - Complete the vocabulary and collocation tasks independently.
 - Group the words by topic or word type.
 - Use at least four target words in short sentences about personal information, family and favourite things.
 Challenge group:
 - Add two suitable words to each vocabulary group.
 - Create a short description or dialogue using numbers from teens to thousands.
 - Explain one word choice using a simple example.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Vocabulary matching and gap-fill check.
 - Correct use of target words in short sentences.
 - Exit ticket: write three words related to personal information, family and favourite things.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Grammar: verb be in affirmative, negative and question forms.
 - Grammar: have got for possessions; questions and short answers.
 - Grammar: this, that, these and those.
 - Possession: possessive ’s and possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their).
 Skill Focus:
 - Reading
 - Writing
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
 - Use be and have got to give simple personal information.
 - Use demonstratives and possessive forms to identify people and objects.
 Skills:
 - Reading: Read model sentences and recognise the correct grammar form.
 - Writing: Complete and write short sentences and questions with the target forms.
 - Speaking: Ask and answer short questions using the target grammar in a familiar context.
 Value:
 - Check language carefully before submitting work.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Underline the target form in the model sentences.
 - Choose the correct form using a grammar box or sentence frame.
 - Build short sentences with verb be in affirmative, negative and question forms from prompts.
 Core group:
 - Complete the grammar exercises independently.
 - Write short affirmative, negative and question forms where relevant.
 - Use verb be in affirmative, negative and question forms in a short pair-check activity.
 Challenge group:
 - Write four original sentences using the target grammar.
 - Find and correct simple grammar mistakes.
 - Use the target grammar in a short text about personal information, family and favourite things.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Grammar exercise accuracy.
 - Short sentence transformation or completion task.
 - Exit ticket using the target grammar.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Functional language: greetings and introductions.
 - Questions about age, birthday, country, town, family, pets, favourite colour and hobbies.
 - Useful expressions for giving personal information.
 Skill Focus:

 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
 - Use greetings and introductions politely.
 - Ask and answer simple personal questions.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Listen to short model conversations and identify the correct order.
 - Speaking: Take part in a short interview about personal information.

items.activities:
Support group:
 - Listen to or read the model language and repeat key expressions.
 - Use question prompts and sentence frames during pair work.
 - Rehearse once before changing roles.
 Core group:
 - Ask and answer all prompts about personal information, family and favourite things.
 - Use the Useful Expressions box and give short complete answers.
 - Change roles and complete the task with a second partner.
 Challenge group:
 - Add two relevant follow-up questions.
 - Give one reason or extra detail in each answer.
 - Use a simple checklist to give peer feedback.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Pair-speaking checklist.
 - Use of target questions and answers.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
- Melting point, boiling point, property, boiling and evaporation.
- Changes of state caused by heating and cooling.
- Differences between boiling and evaporation.
- Sentence patterns for comparing and reporting results.
Skills Focus:
- Reading
- Speaking
- Writing
items.sb:
Resources:
- Open the Teacher Guide first for the teaching flow and materials.
- Use the Student Handout during the lesson.
- Refer to the Teacher Handout for source content and original activities.
- Teachers may flexibly adapt the Teacher Guide and Student Handout to suit students’ needs while maintaining the learning outcomes and safety requirements.

Week 1_U2.1_Change of state
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Define melting point, boiling point and property.
- Describe changes of state caused by heating and cooling.
- Compare boiling and evaporation using accurate Science language.
- Report temperatures using °C.
- Write a conclusion based on results.
Skills:
- Reading: identify key definitions and information in short Science texts and tables.
- Speaking: compare boiling and evaporation and explain observations.
- Writing: record results and present them in a table and bar chart.
Value:
- Develop accuracy, careful observation and honesty when recording results.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Provide a vocabulary bank and sentence frames.
- Use a partially completed comparison table.
- Provide prepared graph axes and labels.
Core group:
- Complete the comparison table and particle drawings.
- Record practical results and complete the bar chart.
- Write a conclusion using class data.
Challenge group:
- Explain why the amount of a substance does not change its melting point.
- Justify conclusions using specific evidence.
items.assess:
- Vocabulary matching task.
- Boiling and evaporation comparison table.
- Practical results table.
- Bar chart and written conclusion.
- Exit Ticket.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Vocabulary: Phrases for introducing someone (this is..., nice to meet you).
 - Expressions: Questions to ask a new friend at school.
 Skill Focus:
 - Listening
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Use everyday phrases to introduce a friend to someone else.
 - Ask and answer questions about school friends and habits.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Listen to a short dialogue about introducing a new friend.
 - Reading: Read quiz questions about being a good friend at school.
 - Speaking: Practice introducing people and interviewing classmates about school friendship.
 Value:
 - Develop a positive and friendly attitude towards new classmates.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Listen and repeat the introduction dialogue with teacher help.
 - Tick the suitable questions to ask a new friend from a given list.
 Core group:
 - Work in groups to practice introducing a friend to someone else.
 - Read the quiz and answer the questions individually.
 - Take turns to interview a partner using the quiz questions.
 Challenge group:
 - Write one or two extra questions to ask a new friend and share with the class.
 - Role-play a real-life introduction situation at school fluently.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during group work.
 - Peer assessment during the introduction role-play.
 - Checking completion of the quiz answers.
 - Exit ticket: Write down two questions you can use to make new friends.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Reading about different school types and facilities.
 - Discussing favourite schools and reasons.
 Skill Focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Talk about different schools and give reasons for choosing them.
 Skills:
 - Reading: Read short passages about three schools to find specific information.
 - Speaking: Talk about which school you like or do not like and give reasons.

 - Show a positive attitude towards their own school and other schools
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match the school names with correct pictures.
 - Complete sentences with given details from the texts with teacher help.
 Core group:
 - Read the texts and complete the gap-fill sentences.
 - Answer comprehension questions about the three schools.
 - Fill in the table and discuss school choices with a partner.
 Challenge group:

items.assess:
- Teacher observation during pair discussion.
 - Checking reading task answers.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Vocabulary: words and phrases related to school life (uniform, favourite teacher, homework, library, biology lesson, classroom, farm, Vietnamese).
 - Listening strategy: predicting and listening for specific information.
 - Writing focus: writing a short paragraph about one's school.
 Skill Focus:
 - Listening
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Understand and use words and phrases related to school life.
 - Write a short paragraph (40–50 words) about their school using guided questions.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Listen to a talk about Janet's school and identify specific information.
 - Writing: Answer questions and write a short paragraph about their school.
 Value:
 - Develop love and pride in their school.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Predict the answers before listening using picture cues.
 - Complete the listening tasks with teacher support.
 - Answer the guided questions using key words.
 Core group:
 - Listen and choose the correct answers.
 - Complete the writing questions independently.
 - Write a 40–50-word paragraph about their school using the given prompts.
 Challenge group:
 - Add more details to make the paragraph more interesting.
 - Share their paragraph with the class and respond to classmates' questions.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during listening and writing activities.
 - Listening comprehension tasks (multiple choice).
 - Writing checklist (content, vocabulary, grammar, organisation).
 - Peer feedback on the writing.
 - Final paragraph submission

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Vocabulary: weddings, family members and personal belongings.
 - Listening focus: choosing the correct option and listening for specific details.
 - Exam strategy: use pictures and instructions to predict the answer type.
 Skill Focus:
 - Listening
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
 - Understand familiar words about a wedding and family.
 - Identify specific people and objects in a short conversation.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Listen to a short conversation and match family members with items.
 - Speaking: Compare answers and discuss a wedding, family members and personal belongings with a partner using simple questions and answers.
 Value:
 - Listen carefully and wait for all the information.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Preview the pictures, names and key words before listening.
 - Listen twice and complete the easier items first.
 - Check answers using the task clues with teacher support.
 Core group:
 - Predict the type of information needed in each item.
 - Complete the listening task and compare answers with a partner.
 - Listen again to confirm specific details.
 Challenge group:
 - Note one extra detail for each speaker or situation.
 - Write two simple questions about the recording.
 - Complete a simple note table with the extra details.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Listening task score.
 - Accuracy of specific-detail answers.
 - Teacher check of the listening strategy used.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Video topic: working dogs and the jobs they do.
 - Vocabulary: pet, police dog, guide dog, guard dog, carer dog and mountain rescue dog.
 - Listening-viewing focus: identifying details and completing a summary.
 Skill Focus:
 - Listening
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
 - Use simple words to name working dogs and their jobs.
 - Give a basic opinion about how dogs help people.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Watch and identify the jobs and actions of different working dogs.
 - Reading: Read the viewing statements and summary about working dogs and the jobs they do to identify the details needed.
 - Speaking: Answer a simple Ideas Focus question about helpful animals.
 Value:
 - Appreciate animals that help people.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Preview the pictures and key words before watching.
 - Watch twice and complete the true/false or matching items.
 - Use visual clues to check answers.
 Core group:
 - Complete the before-, while- and after-watching tasks.
 - Correct false statements using information from the video.
 - Discuss one Ideas Focus question about working dogs and the jobs they do.
 Challenge group:
 - Give a three-sentence summary of the video.
 - Compare the video topic with a familiar example of working dogs and the jobs they do.
 - Create one extra question for classmates.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Before/while/after-watching task.
 - Accuracy of true/false or gap-fill answers.
 - Short oral response to the Ideas Focus question.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Text type: a personal description.
 - Language Focus: be, have got, like and love.
 - Linkers: and, but, also, too and however.
 - Writing length: 25–35 words for the exam task.
 Skill Focus:
 - Reading
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
 - Use simple personal information and favourite-things language in a short description.
 - Connect ideas with basic linkers.
 Skills:
 - Reading: Read two model descriptions and identify useful information and language.
 - Writing: Write a short personal description with clear basic details.
 Value:
 - Present personal information honestly and respectfully.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Identify the parts of the model text with teacher support.
 - Plan ideas using a word bank and sentence starters.
 - Write the text using a guided frame.
 Core group:
 - Write a short text using the model and Useful Expressions.
 - Use a personal description accurately in the first draft.
 - Check content, spelling and punctuation with a checklist.
 Challenge group:
 - Add two relevant details beyond the basic prompts.
 - Improve the draft by varying simple sentence beginnings.
 - Exchange drafts and make one useful revision after peer feedback.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during class activities.
 - Guided writing product.
 - Writing checklist: content, target language, spelling and punctuation.
 - Teacher or peer feedback on one revision.

Language Use:
 - Use familiar personal and family vocabulary to understand short texts and audio.
 - Correct answers by matching people with personal details and favourite things.
 Skills:
 - Reading: Read two short family texts and correct Right/Wrong answers using evidence.
 - Listening: Listen again and match family members with their favourite possessions.

 - Check evidence before changing an answer.

 - Write one extra detail about each person from the texts or audio.

Week 2_U2.1_Fair testing and gases
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Identify changed, controlled and measured variables.
- Describe a safe and logical fair-test method.
- Make a prediction and give a scientific reason.
- Explain that gases take up space and have mass.
- Use observations as evidence.
Skills:
- Listening: follow explanations, demonstrations and safety instructions.
- Speaking: discuss variables, methods and practical findings.
- Writing: complete a fair-test plan and record observations accurately.
Value:
- Demonstrate responsibility, teamwork and safe behaviour during practical work.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Provide a fair-test planning template and sentence frames.
- Give step-by-step practical instructions.
- Assign clear group roles.
Core group:
- Complete the fair-test plan independently.
- Record measurements and observations.
- Answer questions using practical evidence.
Challenge group:
- Identify additional control variables.
- Suggest improvements to make the investigation more reliable.
- Evaluate the strength of the evidence.
items.assess:
- Retrieval questions.
- Completed fair-test plan.
- Practical measurement and observation records.
- Evidence-based answers.
- Individual reflection.
- Exit Ticket.

 - Work in groups to design a dream school.
